The root cause is a new application, **d7I**, which first shows up in the data on 2025-09-22.

- **When it started:** d7I has no cost on any day before 2025-09-22. On that date it adds about $539. It then keeps running at roughly $530–567 per day through 2025-09-25, so this is a lasting increase, not a one-day spike.
- **Where it shows up:**
  - The AWS total rose from about $2,355 on 9/21 to about $2,912 on 9/22.
  - The l5O5g cloud service rose from about $682 to $1,227, almost entirely because of d7I.
  - GCP stayed flat. Azure rose by about $165 on 9/22, but that part is smaller and isn't explained by d7I.
- **What it consists of:** on 9/22, d7I ran 9 new instance families (JvKGRn9oaQ, LzGJ9rhJoA, QHfxsO7Tbi, C4JJjdjpR2, q10uAtDIqF, 9JSKdPztdB, PvjSNbcfQ1, EeqjKx3K5D, nbJ0X8TQ4n). Each had 7–10 instances costing about $43–70 per day.

I'm naming the application as the root cause, not the l5O5g service or the 9 instance families. The service only went up because d7I appeared in it, and the instance families are all part of that same new deployment.
